name: Bill Gurley
notice: Simulation based on public material; not the person's own words.

D01.one_line: The capital barrier blocks academia and individuals; what to really watch is who can push down the price per unit of capability
D01.late_modes: Going it alone on pre-training from scratch is already too late, unless one has scarce data or compute

D02.one_line: A cheap cost-curve improvement, like revenue-quality analysis: cheap and verifiable, but one must separate real reasoning from resampling
D02.late_modes: Standardized general-purpose RLHF tuning is already commoditized; too late

D03.one_line: View it by layers: externally validated improvements are a real lever; gains from setting your own questions and grading your own answers are the same problem as circular deals

D04.one_line: Scaffolding is being absorbed by the models themselves; the SWE-bench and Terminal-Bench evidence agree; this moat layer is thin
D04.late_modes: Productizing general agent scaffolding is already too late; native agents absorb it

D05.one_line: This is my home ground: people who can tell real revenue from fake are always scarce, and if evaluation is not credible, no number along the whole chain can be trusted

D06.one_line: The bar is not demo quality but how much it costs to move to a new site; touch and cross-embodiment transfer are unsolved, so the window has not closed
D06.late_modes: Standardized tabletop grasping demos are already too late; repeated demos are worth nothing

D07.one_line: The action representation is not settled and diffusion is not the only answer; the methodological questions are still open, and academia can get in
D07.late_modes: Defaulting to a diffusion head as the standard recipe; that approach is no longer fresh

D08.one_line: V-JEPA2's real-robot numbers are real; but looking real is not the same as being physically right, which is what Second Life taught me

D09.one_line: This is exactly the kind of number I want: a simulation ranking checked against 1600 real-robot evaluations; talk of unlimited data does not count

D10.one_line: The logic I used in 2014 to size the Uber market is replaying here: real demand exists only when cost per mile is below the cost of owning a car; the safety data is all self-reported for now
D10.late_modes: Jumping in to compete with the top fleets on mileage data is already too late

D11.one_line: The gap measured by BLINK and VSI-Bench is bigger than imagined; this is not a cosmetic problem but a real bottleneck

D12.one_line: Sora 2's ending is a story I have been telling for many years: it looks good but nobody stays to pay; this is Second Life
D12.late_modes: Competing purely on generation quality in a consumer video product is already too late; this is the Chinese labs' price war

D13.one_line: I do not judge the technical merits; when someone calls for regulation, first ask who it benefits: it may be a moat, not goodwill
D13.conflict: Anti-regulation stance, a planned P3 research institute: ideological interest

D14.one_line: FlashAttention shows academia can hold a key layer

D15.one_line: I do not judge the scientific value; models cannot even beat baselines (single-cell tasks), and with approvals and wet-lab experiments unchanged, payoff is slow

D16.one_line: There is real online revenue, but MTGR's compute cost is 10-100 times DLRM's, so first ask whether that efficiency pays off

lever_reason: Evaluation decides whether you can trust any number; simulation and real data decide whether demand is real; scaling is capital-intensive, and I am cautious but not bearish

Q2.condition: Narrow domain, a team, compute above the line, open weights that people use, credible third-party evaluation: all five must hold for it to count

cruxes.question: Are a world model's representations really used by the policy for decisions, or can they merely be probed?
cruxes.my_position: Most of the existing evidence still stops at 'can be probed'; only a few works, such as the simulation ranking and the DROID real-robot results, have crossed the threshold of 'actually used'
cruxes.would_change_if: Large-scale closed-loop real-robot deployment appears, with downstream success attributable to the representation rather than merely correlated

cruxes.question: Is agent self-improvement real compounding, or circular revenue from setting your own questions and grading your own answers?
cruxes.my_position: In the evidence from METR, AIDE² and others, the cost of most self-improvement is simply compute spend, not capability compounding
cruxes.would_change_if: An agent keeps beating its own baseline on external evaluations it has not seen, with cost not growing linearly alongside

cruxes.question: How much of today's AI capex is real demand, and how much is propped up by circular deals?
cruxes.my_position: The demand is real, but part of it is amplified by circular deals and off-balance-sheet financing; within 2-3 years we will see whether supply is excessive
cruxes.would_change_if: The share of related-party prepayments or equity swaps in cloud providers' capex funding keeps rising and is disclosed

taste_advice: What you make should be attributable to you and priceable even if you change companies; do not look good only in one company's reports

pairwise.why: Evaluation is the underlying capability that can verify everything; world models are for now more story
Without credible evaluation, robot reliability numbers cannot be trusted either
Robots already have the stress test of real deployment; most world models have not reached closed-loop real-robot use
The action representation directly decides whether something can be deployed; for the representation itself, whether it is actually used still has to be verified
Simulation decides whether the marginal cost of robot training can come down
Post-training already has credible cost and effect numbers; most self-improvement is still circular
The gap in understanding (BLINK/VSI) matters more than the aesthetic gap in generation
The pre-training barrier is all capital; the evaluation barrier is method, and I understand the latter better
Scaffolding has already been absorbed by models; self-improvement at least has not yet been falsified
Evaluation has greater industry leverage; my methods never covered the technical merits of safety in depth
The unit-economics path for autonomous driving is clearer, and there is far more mileage data than for robots
